transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we dive into the design review, I want to make sure we're all on the same page. We've got two options on the table for the Soundstage 3 courtyard set — a masonry build or a modular painted-timber approach. The approved construction budget is $180,000, and fabrication can't begin until we've completed this review and I've signed off on the final plan. I'd like to hear from each of you — structural, permits, stunt, and insurance — so we can weigh the trade-offs and I can make a decision. Let's start with structural: what are the implications of each option from your side?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical structural finding before we go further. My load test yesterday found that the masonry courtyard option would exceed Soundstage 3's 600 kilograms-per-square-meter floor limit — so that option is not viable as designed. The modular painted-timber design does pass, but only if we install a 30-millimeter load-spreading deck. I should also note that my written report is still working through the engineering queue and hasn't been formally distributed yet, but I wanted to make sure this information is on the table during this review.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share what I confirmed with the local heritage-permit office this morning. The approved facade may be no wider than exactly 8 meters, and on-stage masonry cutting is prohibited. I should also note that the permit clerk's email has not yet been added to the production file, but these constraints are confirmed and in effect.
